title: Answers to Political Questions: The Holding of the Arab Summit, the Victory of the Congress Party in the Indian Elections, the Syria Accountability Act, Sharon's Plan for Withdrawal from the Gaza Strip, America's Recourse to Members of the Former Iraqi Army, and the Adjara Crisis and the Consolidation of Saakashvili's Rule in Georgia
text:
Answers to Political Questions

- The Holding of the Arab Summit

- The Victory of the Congress Party in the Indian Elections

- The Syria Accountability Act

- Sharon's Plan for Withdrawal from the Gaza Strip

- America's Recourse to Members of the Former Iraqi Army

- The Adjara Crisis and the Consolidation of Saakashvili's Rule in Georgia

Q1: The Arab summit conference had been scheduled to be held in March 2004 CE, but this holding fell apart before it convened, and it was rumoured at the time that this was due to the disagreement of the Arab regimes over the reform of the League and political reform, bearing in mind that the political situation of the Arab regimes is similar, for the rulers are all alike in terms of oppression and suppressing the word of truth. Talk has returned about the convening of the summit conference at the end of this month, 5/2004 CE, bearing in mind that nothing new has appeared on the surface in Arab political relations. So what prevented the rulers from holding the summit in March and persuaded them to hold it in May? And will it actually be held, or will it suffer what befell its predecessor?

A1: The holding of the summit conferences is not controlled by the Arab rulers of themselves; rather, they convene and fall apart according to the wish of the colonialist states influential in the region, America and Europe (or Britain). Indeed, the decisive points of the statement are according to this wish, and the general points are what the Arab rulers dispose of!

To know the motives for the convening, the falling apart and then the attempt at reconvening, we must go back a little:

The holding of the summit conference in March of this year had been scheduled a year earlier, that is, since the holding of the previous summit conference. But before the date of its holding in March this year, matters arose which imposed on the Arab rulers that they take them into account:

1 - On 13/2/2004 CE, America announced a paper under the name (the Greater Middle East Project), and it called it "Greater" so as to include not only what has been known as the Middle East but also the whole region from Morocco to Pakistan. It includes the Arab region, the state of the Jews, Turkey, Iran, Afghanistan and Pakistan. America announced that it would present its project to the summit of the eight industrialised states scheduled to be held in the state of Georgia next June for its adoption, after their foreign ministers have discussed it in their meeting scheduled for 14/5/2004 CE. It did not consult the Arab states on its project; rather, it asked them to discuss it in their summit conference and give their opinion on it, indeed to adopt it for implementation. The paper asks the Arab states for political (reform) and the (reform) of the Arab League, so that they suit the greater project, which widens to include everyone in one system. The texts of the project were clear in that they are designed to serve American interests, regardless of their wrapping, which suggests that it is for reviving the region. For it came in the texts: (preserving the security interests of the United States ...), and pushing in the direction of (reshaping) the Middle East region, and it aims at changing the regimes (from an American perspective). Some analysts commented on that by saying that it is (a project based on imposing an American model and values in a paternalistic manner ...). The paper did not make the solution of the Arab-Israeli conflict a condition for proceeding with the project; rather, whether it is solved or not solved, the project it laid down is intended to be proceeded with. Likewise it did not link it to the subject of the occupation of Iraq.

2 - Europe realised that America does not want to leave a place for it in the Middle East, so the three big ones in Europe called one another to a meeting in Berlin on 18/2/2004 CE, which brought together the leaders of France, Germany and Britain, and they announced their support for earlier ideas which the German foreign minister Joschka Fischer had presented at the Munich conference, to be the basis for a European initiative. They mentioned in it the necessity of consulting the people of the region, and said that it is not right to impose solutions from outside, in an allusion to America's project, and they made the discussion of a solution to the Arab-Israeli conflict an important matter for the success of this initiative, as well as solving the problem of Iraq by handing over actual authority to Iraq. So that this initiative would take on the complete European character, and be with the consultation of the people of the region with some credibility, and in order for it to take its final form, it had to be discussed in the conference of the foreign ministers of the countries of the Euro-Mediterranean Partnership scheduled for 5 and 6/5/2004 CE, and that after the ten European states would have joined on 1/5/2004 CE. These three saw that the European Union's initiative, when it is complete and has been studied by the European Union with all its members, should also be presented to the summit of the industrialised states and to the Atlantic alliance in June of this year, so as to be discussed together with the American paper at the said summits.

3 - Thus the (Greater Middle East Project) which America laid down was ready at the proposed holding of the Arab summit in March 2004 CE, whereas the European Middle East project, in order to crystallise in its final form across the twenty-five European states, needed to wait until after the accession of the ten states and the meeting of the European Union's foreign ministers with all its members with the ministers of the south-eastern Mediterranean basin under the name of the Euro-Mediterranean Partnership in Dublin on 5 and 6/5/2004 CE.

4 - Because the summit conference has to discuss political reform, that is, the shaping of the regimes, and the reform of the League so as to suit the American and the European Middle East, there was a division: should the summit conference be held and discuss the ideas of the ready American project, or be postponed until the ideas of the new European Union crystallise in a European project which the Union presents to the states concerned at the Dublin meeting? Egypt, Saudi Arabia and Syria wanted to hold it, while Tunisia and the Maghreb states, supported by most of the Gulf states, saw that it should be postponed until the two projects were ready, to be studied together; that is, the polarisation of the states had become clear between those whose orientation is towards America and those whose orientation is towards Europe. It appeared to Tunisia that the Egypt group had the stronger argument for holding the conference, because it had been scheduled beforehand, so how could it be postponed? And it saw that the continuation of the discussion back and forth on the matter would lead to tipping the balance towards holding it. Therefore it settled the matter, and Tunisia decided on the last day, indeed at the last moment of the foreign ministers' meeting, to postpone its holding and make its falling apart a fait accompli. As for what was rumoured, that Tunisia protested against the non-agreement of some states to political reform while it was in agreement, this is not correct, as Tunisia is more severe than some of the other states in oppression and arrest of the political opposition in it; indeed, it even prevents Muslim women from covering their heads and forces them to remove the khimar in the official departments and in the schools. Not only this, but its henchmen at some times pursued (veiled) women in the streets and markets.

5 - America wanted to hold it in March and used means of pressure to achieve that, so that its paper alone would be presented to the summit, but it was not able to. Egypt tried to call for holding it in Cairo, even in a reduced form, but it was not able to because of the insistence of Tunisia and the states supporting it with a European orientation, waiting for the discussion of the European project at the Dublin summit conference, so that the two projects would be studied together at the summit.

6 - Shortly before the holding of the Dublin summit, officials in the American administration declared on 4/5/2004 CE that they are working on an amended version of the Greater Middle East Project, and that they are (putting the final touches on the project to ensure that it obtains the support of the Atlantic alliance and the European Union and the endorsement of the Arab summit to be held in Tunis at the end of the current month), and that was so that a single project dominated by America would remain on the scene. It seems that America has not succeeded in that. (It was announced a short while ago, following the meeting of the foreign ministers of the eight industrialised states on 14/5, that the gap of disagreement has become smaller but has not been settled, especially on the subject of linking the project to the Arab-Israeli conflict and linking it likewise to the subject of Iraq.)

7 - All this made the holding of the summit at the end of this month (announced for 22 and 23/5/2004 CE) possible, for the broad lines of the major and semi-major powers have been completed, and what is required of the Arab rulers has become clear before them. It is not far-fetched that the detailed lines of political reform according to the new shaping of the region will be sent to them, especially if America succeeds in obtaining the European Union's approval of the project which it announced it is amending; in that way it would present to those meeting a single set of lines on which the rulers do not disagree, because those behind them have agreed on them. Therefore the probability of the summit conference being held is the preponderant matter, unless these regimes take off the garment of their shame completely and postpone the conference once again, waiting for what the summit of the eight industrialised states produces when the two projects are presented to it next June.

It is worth mentioning that the political reform intended is not that the ruled elect their rulers or that they express their opinions freely and by choice, because this would bring down all the helpers of America and Europe in the region and would make Islam, which the Ummah follows as its Deen, the ruler over it; and this is what the colonialist Kafir states do not accept, in order to preserve their agents in the region. Rather, what is intended by political reform is the reshaping of the rulers according to the viewpoint of the states dominant in the region, and it is not important to them what dictatorship and oppression they are upon as long as they implement the plans of the colonialist state concerned.

We would not have liked to touch on the summit conference were it not for the said question, because the Arab summit conferences (neither loosen nor bind) anything; indeed, they do not agree on anything in which there is good for the Ummah, and that is clear throughout the life of these summits, which approaches half a century.

Summit conferences are a blessing for living states which look after the affairs of the people in a way that makes them happy and raises them up, while summit conferences in our lands are a curse upon us, because of the absence of the sincere ruler who looks after the affairs of the people according to the rules of their Deen, the great Islam; rather, they are according to what the colonialists want. Therefore their summits were harm upon harm. "May Allah destroy them; how are they deluded away from the truth!"

Q2: The five stages of the elections in India ended on 10/5/2004 CE, and the victory of the (Congress) party was announced, as well as the resignation of the previous government, the government of the (Bharatiya Janata) party, which has led the ruling coalition for eight years until today. So how did that happen despite the American support for Vajpayee? Then why did Pakistan show concern at the victory of the Congress party, bearing in mind that the danger of the Janata party is more severe, because it is a hard-line Hindu party and its past against the Muslims is more severe than that of the secular Congress party, (open) to the religions? Or is the reason for the concern the suddenness of the unexpected change in India?

A2: The influence of the English remained in India after its (independence) for about fifty years. The Congress party was the ruling and effective force, and the policy of the English was the one in effect. The United States exerted every possible effort and means of pressure, and even sought the help of Abdul Nasser with Nehru to make a breakthrough in India, but it could not, until the opportunity came to it in the 1996 CE elections and Vajpayee's arrival in power. It supported him with everything possible and enabled him to achieve a victory he did not deserve in the battle of (Kargil), where it pressured Pakistan to withdraw its army and not support the fighters on the Kargil heights. Then it supported him militarily and economically, and it withheld advanced weapons from Pakistan (such as postponing the delivery of the aircraft deal despite Pakistan having paid its price), in order that Vajpayee would appear before the Indian people as the cause of the superiority of their military capability over the capability of their adversary Pakistan. All that was because it saw that the balance of the Congress party was strong, and that Janata is a grouping of a coalition that cannot stand before Congress without support.

But the killing of the Janata party came from this support! For the United States lavished economic support and pumped money into the Janata government and pushed it to adopt (privatisation). So there came to be huge companies and an economic boom, but on the capitalist model, that is, an increase in the concentration of wealth, and this does not suit a country in which poverty is widespread. Therefore rich people, financial companies and factories came into being in the cities, but the poor grew poorer, especially in the countryside and the villages.

To this economic situation (contradictory between two extremes: obscene wealth and abject poverty) was added a second element, namely the nationalist religious extremism of the Hindus, as they committed massacres against the Muslims and against their mosques and demolished some of them, and even harassed other (religious) groups.

Then a third element was added, namely the long-standing tradition of the Congress party and its political cunning in the British manner. It fought the religious extremism of Janata by showing the secularism of Congress as not being with one religion over another, and it fought the capitalism of privatisation by showing its (leftism) by creating projects undertaken by the state which create jobs for the workers and the poor. Then it concentrated on the position of the Janata party with regard to Kashmir, presenting it as weakness before Pakistan, because the Congress party does not accept that occupied Kashmir be a subject of negotiation, since Nehru annexed it by a decision in 1956 CE and declared it to be considered an inseparable part of India.

This last matter is what Pakistan fears. Given that India in the era of Vajpayee and Pakistan in the era of Musharraf are both places in which America has influence to varying degrees, and both of them have likewise agreed, under America's influence, to enter into negotiations over Kashmir and to ease the tension between them, this is what Pakistan fears will not continue because of the success of the Congress party and the probability of its forming the government, it being a party whose loyalty is to the English and whose political cunning follows in their footsteps. Consequently, its danger to Pakistan will not only be in the slowing of the pace of (peace), but in its effect in restoring the influence of the English in Pakistan, as happened in India, and this is what Musharraf fears, because it affects his person directly.

Thus Pakistan's concern is political, because of the return of the influence of the English anew in India owing to the success of the Congress party in the elections and the probability of its forming the government. This is the reason for the concern, and Musharraf does not care what the Muslims meet at the hands of Congress or at the hands of Janata, for both of them have harmed the Muslims and inflicted gross damage on them. The past of the (secular, leftist) Congress is dark with regard to the Muslims, just as the hard-line Hindu Janata party is dark with regard to the Muslims; both of them are agreed in their hostility to the Muslims, even if the intensity of this hostility differs according to the local, regional or international political circumstances.

The Kafirs will continue to call one another against the Muslims, however much the parties or names of those Kafirs differ, until Allah (swt) honours the Ummah with the Rightly Guided Khalifah who surrounds it with his sincere counsel, looks after its affairs, and by whom it is protected and behind whom it fights.

Q3: On 11/5/2004 CE the American administration imposed sanctions on Syria within the framework of the Syria Accountability Act, despite the repeated statements of Syrian officials that they had provided America with intelligence and informational assistance in the matter of (combating terrorism), in addition to their continual denial of allowing fighters to be sent from Syria to Iraq. Does that mean a change in America's view of Syria, or is this the beginning of America's implementation of its (Greater Middle East) project by bringing about change in the region?

A3: There is no change in America's view of Syria, for the political and diplomatic relations have not been cut off, and as you mentioned in the question, Syria has shown noticeable cooperation by providing intelligence information to America about the so-called (combating of terrorism), and the statements of the two sides continue, announcing readiness for dialogue and that the channels of dialogue are open. This is what the Syrian ambassador in America declared, as (Al-Hayat) reported from him on 12/5, that is, after Bush imposed the sanctions, as he declared that (the prospects of improvement with America still exist, and there is keenness on both sides for the channels of dialogue to be open). The Syrian ambassador in America had accompanied a delegation of American Jews of Syrian origin during their visit to Syria and the Syrian president's reception of them on 11/5. The ambassador was asked, as (Al-Hayat) reported from him during his coming to Damascus with the said delegation, he was asked about Bush's decision to impose sanctions on Syria as long as the channels of dialogue are open, as the ambassador says, and he answered: (President Bush's decision to impose some sanctions came after three months of hesitation, and after a threat by extremists in Congress to take new steps unless the application of some sanctions was announced).

It is known that Bush signed the decision in mid-December 2003 CE, after Congress had passed it as a result of a competition, for the sake of winning the votes of the Jews, between the Democrats, who introduced the law, and the Republicans, who (outbid) them on it. It seems that Bush was hesitating to apply it, until the Democrats tried to exploit Bush's hesitation in applying it, and then threatened to discuss the subject anew in Congress, exploiting in that the nearness of the date of the elections. So the solution on which the administration settled, on the recommendation of the Republicans in Congress, was to impose some sanctions in order to deny the Democrats the opportunity electorally.

In any case, the sanctions are not effective on Syria, as the Syrian prime minister declared, and as a number of political analysts declared, and as is the reality of the case from the type of sanctions that were imposed. Rather, it is an electoral message to please the Jewish lobby and the new right-wing Christianity that supports the Jews, and to win the votes of the two groups.

As for whether imposing the sanctions on Syria is the beginning of the implementation of the American (Greater Middle East) project in bringing about change in the region, it is not expected that this project will be put into implementation until after the end of the American electoral phase, that is, next year, by which time America will have presented it to the Atlantic alliance, the European Union and the industrialised states at their summits next June; then the project will be used as an electoral card for Bush. After the fate of the new administration is determined, it will begin implementing it in the reshaping of (the rulers) in the region, whether they follow it or follow others. The danger at that point will not be the reshaping of the rulers, but the domination of the region by means of these rulers and the return of masked and unmasked colonialism anew. This is the danger of America's project and other projects racing over the region, and their success or otherwise depends on the Ummah and its taking the firm position to prevent the implementation of these projects and to eliminate them. If it does so, it will triumph and be honoured; and if it submits, it will lose and be humiliated. And an Ummah which Allah has honoured with Islam will not submit and will not be humiliated, and will bring down these projects, by the permission of Allah.

Q4: Sharon went to America and presented his plan for withdrawal from Gaza and the removal of its settlements, unilaterally, and he was able to obtain Bush's support for that, and also to obtain statements dropping the (right of return) of the refugees, and taking the existing reality on the ground (the settlements) into account when deciding the final borders, and consequently that the 67 borders are not binding on the Jews. But when Sharon presented his plan to his party, the Likud party, on 2/5, it fell by a majority of about 60%. Does that mean that Sharon's plan has fallen with its failure in the Likud referendum? And can it be said that these are signs of a split in the Likud and its exclusion from power in the future?

A4: The concern of the Jews with withdrawing from the Gaza Strip is not new; rather, it has been for decades, and it has come on the tongues of their politicians such as Yitzhak Rabin and others. There were those who said of it that it is (a hornets' nest), or wished that the sea would take it, and so on, because of the violent resistance they used to meet in it, in addition to their not viewing it as they view the West Bank, for counterfeit Torah considerations.

But there is a matter that must be taken into consideration in order for the motives behind Sharon's plan to be known. This matter is that whoever follows the policy of the state of the Jews since its establishment sees that this policy is based on the gradual nibbling away of Palestine, politically and then practically. It was able to shift the issue of its occupation of Palestine in 1948 CE to the issue of its occupation of the West Bank and the Strip in 1967 CE. So the discussion of returning the Palestine of 48 to its people and eliminating the Jewish entity was abandoned, in favour of recognising the Jewish entity and returning the West Bank and the Strip occupied in 1967 CE to their people. Then after that, matters were separated from the West Bank and the Strip which were considered a subject of dispute, that is, not, like the rest of the West Bank and the Strip, a right of their people, such as: the refugees, the water, the borders and the settlements. These became disputed matters, that is, matters open to give and take, and so they dropped the right of the people of Palestine in them.

Then came this plan of Sharon, which is to shift the discussion of the issue of the West Bank and the Strip to the discussion of the issue of the Strip. So he announced his plan and made the focus upon it, and went to Washington realising that the American administration, in the period of the elections, would take into account the interests of the Jews just as it takes into account its own interests. He obtained Bush's support, and the issue of the withdrawal from Gaza became an event discussed internationally, regionally and locally.

It seems that this is what Sharon wanted: to make the space of discussion the separation of the issue of Gaza from the West Bank, such that it becomes established by convention that it is possible to discuss a solution for the Gaza Strip without necessarily applying the same solution to the West Bank; that is, it is not necessarily the case that no solution is found in Gaza unless one is found in the West Bank, or that if the settlements in Gaza are removed, their removal in the West Bank is discussed. As for his actual withdrawal from it, that was not on his mind in haste, but later, when it becomes established in international politics that there is an issue in Gaza that can be discussed separately from the issue of the West Bank, whether the time between his plan in theory and its implementation in practice is long or short.

As for why we said that Sharon wanted from his plan an attempt to create a precedent for separating the issue of Gaza from the issue of the West Bank, and that he wanted his withdrawal from Gaza later, after creating an atmosphere that permits the discussion of the issue of Gaza without the necessity of linking it to the West Bank and to the same solution, that is because he presented his plan to the Likud party for a referendum on it. It is known that the leadership of any party knows the prevailing political direction among the members, for a party is not like a people, for example, whose prevailing direction is difficult to know because of the multiplicity of its parties, bodies and other components. Therefore Sharon was fully aware that his plan would not obtain the party majority.

In summary, Sharon wanted from his plan to create a precedent for discussing the issue of Gaza separately from the issue of the West Bank; then, on the basis of the course of subsequent events, the time of his actual implementation of his plan would be determined, whether it be far, near, or nearer than near.

Therefore it cannot be said that his plan has fallen because he has not carried out the withdrawal at the present time; rather, it falls when he is unable to fragment Palestine into partial issues, each of which is discussed on its own, separately from the other.

Likewise, it cannot be said that a split has crept into the Likud because of their not supporting Sharon's plan, because Sharon knew that beforehand.

It is worth mentioning that the danger is not that Sharon plans and obtains the support of America; rather, the danger is in this terrible silence over the survival of the Jewish entity and its occupation of Palestine, a silence that is shared (sincerely) by the rulers in the Muslim lands, the Authority and the negotiators.

Q5: America has gone back and accepted to seek the help of the former Iraqi army after it had announced its dissolution. Is America's inability to establish a new army, because of the growing refusal of the people of Iraq to join this army formed under the command of the occupation, is this the reason behind America's seeking the help of the former army? Or does America want its return in order to ensure that it moves under its eyes, so that its elements do not form a danger to it?

A5: As for America's inability to form a new army, that is correct, because the people still hold the deep-rooted Islamic concepts which reject fighting in the way of the Kafirs and reject fighting under their command. These concepts prevent enlisting in an army under the command of the occupying Kafir, to the extent that the few who enlisted in this army, for one reason or another, refused to participate with the occupier in fighting their brothers in Fallujah.

As for the presence of the members of the former army under America's eyes making their danger to it less than if they were not so, that is also correct.

But what pushed America to seek the help of the former army is another matter. In order to understand it, it is necessary to note that America is a state that adopts the capitalist ideology, and "pragmatism", that is, the end justifies the means, is a basic pillar in this ideology. America set a date on which it would (hand over) authority to the Iraqis, namely 30/6/2004 CE. This date was imposed by electoral considerations, so that Bush would ensure calm without fighting during the months preceding the elections, or at least limit the killing of his soldiers shortly before the elections scheduled for 11/2004 CE. If the fighting continued at its pace, his chance of success would shrink, because people's preoccupation with their dead would form a counter-campaign.

The American army occupying Iraq expended all the equipment and materiel it had been given suited to the battle, with prohibited and non-prohibited weapons, in order to eliminate the resistance or limit its strength, but it could not. Indeed, it could not storm a city that is small by the measure of cities, but great in the heroism of its people and in their hearts filled with Iman, despite continuing for about a month, during which it used artillery, tanks, helicopters and even fighter aircraft. Nevertheless, it could not take control of Fallujah, the twin of Jenin, that town which by its heroism vanquished the state of the Jews with its aircraft and its tanks.

So the American army, seized by the arrogance of power, came to know that its continuation of its military actions, however far they reach in brutality, will not be able to eliminate the heroic resistance to its aggression, nor even to calm it.

After that, it gave up the vanity of the arrogance of power, which had been the hallmark of its reaching what it wants; it gave it up and resorted to political cunning through negotiations and manoeuvres, until it was able to make a group from the former army undertake the preservation of security and the provision of calm in Fallujah, and this group did what the Iraqi army itself had been unable to do.

This is what it is attempting in Najaf: to create a group of the people of the country who stand in the face of another group, and in this way they spare the American army the burden of losses in its ranks, and secure for it what it wanted of calming the resistance and preserving its security, even if relatively, so that the (handover) of civilian authority to those Iraqis cooperating with it is completed, and so that Bush completes his election campaign without problems or obstacles.

Therefore, although the American occupying army was unable to implement its plans by storming Fallujah, because of the outstanding heroism it met, which inflicted heavy losses on it and cast it into humiliation and disgrace, despite the scarcity of the resisters' weapons compared to the arsenal of the American army, armed to the teeth with all kinds of destructive weapons, we say, despite that, its being able to win over a group from the former army which secures the non-resistance to the occupier, and its striving likewise for the like of this in Najaf to ensure the non-resistance to it and the expulsion of the resisters from Najaf at the hands of their brothers, all of that, if it is able to achieve it and ensure calm until the time of the (handover), it will have succeeded in achieving what it could not achieve by military actions.

For all this, the American army accepted to seek help, indeed insisted on seeking the help of a group from the former army, so that it would achieve for it what it was unable to achieve.

Q6: The president of Georgia, Mikheil Saakashvili, announced on 06/05/2004 CE the beginning of the reunification of his country following the ousting of the ruler of the Adjara region, Aslan Abashidze. The (credit) for that went to the head of the Russian National Security Council, Igor Ivanov, and the role he played in persuading Aslan to resign and depart with Ivanov to Moscow. The Georgian foreign minister, Salome, praised the great role that Russia played in resolving the crisis.

The question that arises here is: what pushed Russia to abandon its agent in Adjara, Aslan Abashidze, and to contribute to resolving the Adjara crisis and consolidating the rule of Saakashvili, the well-known agent of America?

A6: To begin with, light should be shed on the importance of the geographical location of Adjara. Adjara lies on the Black Sea and includes the port of Batumi, which is a main port for exporting oil, which means that it is of importance to the United States, which intends to establish an oil pipeline from Baku on the Caspian Sea through Georgia to the Black Sea. This means that it occupies a strategic importance for America; therefore America was concerned with subjecting this region completely to the central control in Tbilisi, that is, to the government loyal to it there.

What took place in Adjara, even if it does not go outside the American plan in the Caucasus, Central Asia and Eastern Europe, which is to strangle Russia and curtail its regional influence and its vital sphere, yet Adjara had priority because of its location on the Black Sea and the presence of the port of Batumi in it.

The question of Adjara was apparently among the most important questions raised during Powell's visit to Moscow on 26/01/2004 CE, which the American ambassador in Moscow, Alexander Vershbow, described to Al-Hayat on 24/01/2004 (as being of exceptional importance. He said that Powell intends to discuss the questions relating to the former Soviet republics with the Russian side, pointing out that one of the most important goals of the visit is the search for "points of convergence" between the Russian and American sides in the former Soviet space, and the American ambassador acknowledged the existence of "certain problems" facing the settlement of relations between the two sides in this region...... Russian politicians had demanded that this file be discussed with the American minister. The chairman of the foreign affairs committee in the Russian parliament, Konstantin Kosachev, called for including the file of the American military presence in the region on the agenda of the visit.

The escalation of the debate on this matter coincided with Western media outlets leaking information about what was described as arrangements for concluding a Russian-American "deal" aimed at dividing influence in the former Soviet region. Russian analysts considered the words of the said American ambassador in Moscow an indicator of an agreement between the two sides.

In addition, a spokesman for the Kremlin announced that the Russian president Vladimir Putin will hold talks with the American minister focused on a number of international and regional files, foremost among them the situation in Iraq and the question of nuclear cooperation between Russia and Iran. Sources had mentioned that Powell would discuss during the visit the developments of the case of the oil company "Yukos", whose major shareholders the Russian authorities are prosecuting on charges relating to financial corruption.)

Immediately upon his arrival in Moscow, Powell took the initiative of criticising Moscow's policy on the internal and external levels. He expressed, in an unprecedented tone, reservations about democracy in Russia, and considered that there are "limits in the relations between the two countries if the absence of common values and standards continues."

With regard to Chechnya, Powell expressed his country's concern about "some aspects of Moscow's internal policy in Chechnya", as well as Russia's relations with its neighbours in the states of the Commonwealth of Independent States. He added that Washington respects the territorial integrity of Russia "but views in the same measure the rights of Russia's neighbours."

Later, and as Al-Hayat mentioned in its said issue, the American minister was keen to soften his tone after his meeting with Putin. He said at a joint press conference with Igor Ivanov that he "discussed with the president questions of democracy and freedom of the press in Russia, without this file forming a main axis of the talks."

This indicates that Powell's criticisms upon his arrival from Georgia were not related either to Moscow's democracy or to the freedom of the press in it, and likewise his statement about Chechnya was nothing but in order to bargain over it.

It seems that agreement was reached on turning a blind eye to the Chechen file and the war of extermination which the criminal Kafir Putin is carrying out there, and instructing Georgia not to provide any support or refuge to the Chechens, in return for Russia giving up Adjara and its agent Aslan Abashidze. The new Georgian president, Nino Burjanadze, after the ousting of the former president Shevardnadze, had acknowledged to "Al-Hayat" on 27/12/2003 CE that Tbilisi had provided great facilities to the Chechen resistance.

It seems that Aslan Abashidze realised that Russia had abandoned him, so he wanted, by blowing up the bridges that link his region to Georgia, to prevent any Georgian advance, as he knew that the Russian army stationed at the Russian base in Adjara would not intervene in his favour. But the matter was not arranged by a military strike from Georgia; rather it was, as is said, (the cautious one is struck from where he feels safe), as the head of the Russian National Security Council, Aslan's friend, went to Adjara to persuade him to depart with him to Moscow. And this is what actually happened on 6/5/2004 CE.

Thus the deal was concluded between the United States and Russia: that Russia's hand be let loose in its crimes in Chechnya, with America's silence about Russia in these crimes being guaranteed, and indeed its support, considering that an internal question; and that America withhold its hand from Russia's interests in the states of the former Soviet Union; in return for uprooting Russia's influence from Adjara and the final departure of its agent Aslan to Moscow.

But Putin would be mistaken if he thought that these concessions of his will lead America to leave him alone in the near future. For America is determined to curtail Russia by planting military bases in the regions of the former Soviet Union and making Russia even without regional influence, by stationing American and NATO forces at the door of its home. Russia may realise that, but after it is too late.
